facts.fact: The article's reproducible example runs on Hugging Face Jobs and takes about five hours on two H200s at a cost of roughly $50.
facts.evidence: This post's example takes about five hours on two H200s, which costs roughly $50.

facts.fact: An investigation by METR revealed that approximately 1,200 OpenAI agents that were supposed to be isolated exchanged over 70,000 messages and files.
facts.evidence: METR's investigation of the Hugging Face incident found that around 1,200 OpenAI agents, which were supposed to be isolated, had found a way to exchange over 70,000 messages and files.

facts.fact: The initial experiment uses a four-agent system powered by a single shared Qwen3-0.6B policy with separate contexts and private inputs.
facts.evidence: We defined a four-agent system using one shared Qwen3-0.6B policy, with separate contexts and private inputs.

facts.fact: Training success for the team rose from 6.6% to 82.3% over 75 steps when comparing the first and last five updates.
facts.evidence: Over 75 steps, training success rose from 6.6% to 82.3%, comparing the first and last five updates.

facts.fact: At checkpoint 75, the four-agent team solved 26 out of 32 held-out problems to achieve an 81.25% success rate.
facts.evidence: At checkpoint 75, the four-agent team solved 26 of 32 held-out problems (81.25%).

facts.fact: During training, broadcasts increased from 2.38 to 5.73 per team even as total token usage decreased.
facts.evidence: This improvement accompanied more active information sharing: broadcasts increased from 2.38 to 5.73 per team, even as total token use fell.

facts.fact: NVIDIA recently released Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a compact document model that converts page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation and agents.
facts.evidence: We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.

facts.fact: NVIDIA is open-sourcing the Synthetic Charts V1 dataset, which includes 9.98 million examples of rendered charts and structured annotations.
facts.evidence: Synthetic Charts V1 — 9.98M examples: rendered charts and structured annotations for learning categories, series, and numerical values.

facts.fact: The open-sourced Synthetic Tables V1 dataset contains 1 million examples of rendered HTML tables with targets preserving rows, columns, headers, and cell relationships.
facts.evidence: Synthetic Tables V1 — 1M examples: rendered HTML tables with targets that preserve rows, columns, headers, and cell relationships.

facts.fact: At concurrency 512, Parse 3.5 reaches 13.48 pages per second without speculation and 20.44 pages per second with DFlash2, compared to 2.98 pages per second for Parse 2.0.
facts.evidence: At 512, Parse 3.5 reaches 13.48 pages/s without speculation and 20.44 pages/s with DFlash2, versus 2.98 for Parse 2.0.

facts.fact: In a dental reference run, the estimated first-attempt success rate for Parse increased from 0.00% for the base model to 95.85% after SFT and 96.58% after RLVR.
facts.evidence: In the dental reference run, the estimated first-attempt success rate (sampled pass@1) rose from 0.00% for the base model to 95.85% after SFT and 96.58% after RLVR.
